Traverse both evidence and artifact dependencies: sources/extractions/renditions, cells/facts/chunks/vectors/relations/aliases, mappings/previews/raw/crops, all storage versions, attempts/orphans/caches and pending output. Cross-document dependent facts/relations/applicability sets become unavailable transactionally before purge; another document's independent evidence survives. Holds retain bytes in restricted custody, never ordinary search.

requirements.section: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.parent: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.text: 4. Retention is C16 root-aware GC, not a standalone superseded TTL. Proposed defaults: online purge≤24 h, crash temp≤24 h, incomplete/rejected quarantine7 d, superseded unheld/unrooted artifacts30 d, backups≤35 d, content-free audit1 y. Accepted originals follow approved records policy. States distinguish access-blocked, tombstoned, online-purged, held, backup-expired; no instantaneous erasure claim.

requirements.section: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.parent: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.text: 5. Restore sealed/offline: verify independent journal/authority anchors and chain/head, replay all intents/tombstones, compare SQL visible heads with independent acknowledged commit checkpoints and obtain current identity/policy/key state, reconcile every store version and semantic/serving root. Missing/corrupt/rolled-back journal or uncertain prior authority death prevents readiness. Journal backup and approved RPO/RTO remain operational requirements; its SQL projection is never the live authority.

requirements.section: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.parent: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.text: Migration compatibility: v1 records never masquerade as v2. Implement strict version-discriminated readers/converters; preserve originals and old extraction blobs, derive new v2 graphs with conversion reports; if missing source/offset/authority, quarantine for review. DB migrations use expand→backfill→validate→switch→contract; avoid destructive rollback. Dual generations run shadow comparisons; C13 corpus serving-profile switch is the model rollback unit, independent of source publication. Retained rollback releases/profiles are C16 roots for their approved window. Rollback cannot revive deleted/unauthorized/expired content. New embedding space uses a separate space-keyed representation (dimension-specific table where necessary), full rebuild and C13 completeness/cutover; recalibrate rank/support policy after encoder/reranker/chunker changes. API major changes get `/v2`; additive optional response fields require reviewed compatibility, never weaken invariant checks.

requirements.section: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.parent: C10 Deletion, recovery, schema evolution and telemetry
requirements.text: Observability event shape: event_id, request/job/attempt IDs, tenant pseudonymous ID, stage/action, outcome, safe error code, auth/corpus/semantic/lease epochs and corpus revision, duration_ms, input/output byte and page counts, bounded queue depth, model/profile opaque IDs, CPU/RSS counters. No source text/query/PII/filenames. Metric labels are fixed low-cardinality stage/outcome/model-profile keys, never document/entity/user IDs. Traces redact bodies/cookies/headers by allowlist and are private. User-visible error strings are Vietnamese. Audit has actor/action/reason/target refs only; review notes live in protected artifacts. Detailed benchmark gold is private; public reports contain aggregate counts/intervals and synthetic examples only.

`ReviewPackage` is an immutable bounded manifest: `package_id, tenant_id, document_id, version_id, extraction_id, rendition_id|null, subject_revision, canonical_hash|null, candidate_manifest_hash, scan_attestation_id, safe_preview_manifest_id, coverage_revision, policy_revision, created_at, expires_at`. `subject_revision` is a monotonic review revision and changes on any candidate/coverage/preview/scan replacement. Before canonical acceptance, candidate IDs and raw offsets are explicitly typed as candidate references, never published evidence IDs. A package can include a rejected extraction for diagnosis but grants no original export. Expiry default15 min; IDs are references, not bearer capabilities. A later package does not mutate an earlier one.

`can_inspect_staged_review(ctx,package,now)` requires live trusted same-tenant principal/membership; **server-provisioned** `inspect_staged` reviewer assignment for this document or restricted-intake custodian group; current clearance at least max(document effective label, package label), department/purpose; nondeleted/no journal deny; matching exact version/extraction and current subject revision; state awaiting_review/staged/accepted-but-unpublished; completed clean scan of the exact source hash with currently accepted scanner/signature policy; verified safe raster/escaped-text preview and bounded manifest. Review assignment does not imply read/search/original rights. Upload receipt visibility never implies inspection. A stale/outdated scan suspends the package pending safe revalidation. Malware/no safe preview gives status only; no unsafe source response as a workaround.

| POST `/documents/{id}/review-packages` | Authorized reviewer requests exact version/extraction and expected subject revision; 201 manifest or 409 stale / safe 503 scan/preview pending. Broker builds safe preview under job limits; request does not run a parser. |
| GET `/review-packages/{package_id}` | Reauthorize; bounded coverage/candidate IDs, safe status and exact identity; no storage keys, raw parser dump or unrelated extraction. |

| GET `/review-packages/{package_id}/evidence/{candidate_id}` | Only listed candidate text/locator, explicitly unaccepted; bounded to256 KiB; never resolvable through ordinary `/evidence` before publication. |
| GET `/review-packages/{package_id}/previews/{preview_id}` | Listed safe page/crop only, no original; per-request S05 dispatch, private/no-store. |

| POST `/documents/{id}/reviews` | Package ID + If-Match subject revision + decision union/reason/idempotency. Recheck current assignment/scan/package/source and all decision dependencies transactionally. Extraction-byte corrections create a new extraction, requiring a new package; semantic decisions follow the explicit canonical-backed staged or published branch below. |

SQL additions: `review_assignments(T,id,document_id,principal_id?|group_id?,capability=inspect_staged|review_semantics|review_classification,purpose_id,valid_from,valid_to?,revision)` with XOR subject, tenant/document/principal/group FKs; `scan_attestations(T,id,document_id,version_id,source_sha256,scanner_revision,signatures_at,verdict,policy_revision,revoked_at?)`; `review_packages` with the fields above and composite ownership FKs plus artifact dependencies. Index assignments by document/subject, packages by document/extraction/subject_revision and scans by version/source hash. Runtime cannot fabricate scan attestations. All content tables keep FORCE RLS. Separate `rag_review_reader` role/policies permit **only** package-member rows through `can_inspect_staged_review`; ordinary `rag_reader` policies have no staged OR exception. Trusted API selects the fixed route role transaction-locally; client cannot select it. Service resolver rechecks identical predicate, field allowlist and gate. Package metadata is itself restricted.

Audit package creation, each inspected candidate/preview, decision, denial and assignment change using actor/purpose/target/package/revision/outcome only. A staged decision records its package hash and decision evidence IDs; a published decision below records its exact published subject/source hash and prior decision IDs, not a package. Publication consumes exact decisions; a review cannot approve different bytes. T01 covers actual-role policy isolation and reviewer revocation; finite documentation examples do not establish RLS enforcement.

Staged semantic decisions retain the package path: after canonical acceptance, `/reviews` may use the same fact_accept/fact_retract/fact_correct/link_accept/link_undo/link_correct branch fields defined below, with package-listed canonical-backed candidate/field/decision IDs, current inspect_staged **and** review_semantics authority, package subject revision and expected semantic epoch/prior decisions. This is a strict staged request variant, not a published-subject fallback. Before canonical acceptance, candidate approval is preliminary only and cannot create accepted fact trust; finalize against exact accepted canonical evidence/new current package. Cross-document secondary dependencies must already be published and independently readable; other staged documents are outside this initial branch. C14 events may exist before publication but published channels still require source publication. Extraction-byte corrections alone require a new extraction/package. This preserves initial fact/link review without broadening ordinary readers or requiring a source to publish before its own review.

Review subjects are a strict discriminated union, not a relaxed staged predicate. `StagedReviewSubject={kind:"staged",package_id,subject_revision}` is valid only on `/reviews`; `PublishedReviewSubject={kind:"published",document_id,version_id,extraction_id,rendition_id,release_id,release_scope:"current"|"history"}` is valid only on `/published-reviews`. The path document must match. Published means the exact immutable release contains this accepted extraction/rendition, not an extraction-state enum or possession of an old package. `current` requires the active source release; `history` additionally requires explicit history capability. A retired source is never silently retargeted. Unknown fields and cross-branch fields reject with422.

`PublishedReviewRequest={subject,expected_semantic_epoch,prior_decision_ids[],decision,reason_code}` plus If-Match `document_revision` and Idempotency-Key. `decision` has required discriminator `kind` and exactly the listed branch fields (notation `tag:{fields}` means `{kind:tag,...fields}`): `fact_accept:{candidate_field_id}`; `fact_retract:{field_id}`; `fact_correct:{field_id,replacement:<C05 candidate observation with exact evidence>}`; `link_accept:{left_observation_id,right_observation_id}`; `link_undo:{link_decision_id}`; `link_correct:{link_decision_id,left_observation_id,right_observation_id}`; `relation_accept:{relation_id,family_heads[]}`; `relation_retract:{relation_decision_id,family_heads[]}`; or `classification_change:{dimension,proposed_value,expected_permission_epoch,approval_decision_ids[]}`. `family_heads[]` is empty for nonfamily relations; family predicates require exact `{family_id,revision,membership_revision,membership_hash}` for every affected family and family-management authority. Their acceptance/retraction embeds the C12 membership transition in the same transaction; a standalone relation event cannot bypass membership invalidation. Server mints replacement observation/decision IDs. Each branch requires exact existing subject/dependency ownership, the exact current prior decisions, at most32 supporting evidence refs and the C08 body limit. Unknown or ambiguous values remain C05 unknown/ambiguous, never forced accepted. Fact acceptance copies a validated canonical-backed candidate into a new human_accepted observation and appends its acceptance event (the unreviewed observation remains historical). Fact correction appends an observation and retract/accept events; link correction appends undo/accept events. Canonical text corrections still create a new extraction; these semantic operations do not.

`can_review_published(ctx,subject,decision,now)` requires current trusted tenant identity, explicit `review_semantics` assignment/capability (or the specific `review_classification` authority), clearance/department/purpose and `can_read_evidence` for the subject and **every** supporting source/observation/decision under current or explicitly historical scope. Sign/upload/staged-inspect alone grants none of these rights. Published evidence is inspected through ordinary authorized `/evidence` and safe `/previews`, never a staged package or implied original export. Assignment changes advance auth epoch. Classification changes retain all existing escalation/downgrade and distinct-approver rules; they use S05 policy mutation, advancing auth/permission epochs and invalidating affected trust, not a fact-event tag pretending to change access.

`fact_correct.replacement` is an ID-free C05 field proposal with exactly `status,value,raw_literal_refs[],candidates[],evidence_ids[],qualifiers[],applicability,scope_components`. Field type is fixed by the target and the server derives the catalog field key for the reviewed scope; value/candidates/qualifiers/applicability use C05's strict unions, and scope_components is C12's versioned scope tuple with explicitly tagged unknown components. Server supplies ownership/IDs/assessment/recorded-time and derives the new scope key; a caller cannot disguise a money/date correction as text or overwrite literal evidence. A known source-confirmed replacement appends human_accepted observation and accept event; unknown/ambiguous/not-applicable replacement closes old trust and records the new unaccepted status **without** an accepted-value row. Changing installment/currency/party/condition therefore retracts the old scoped predicate, rather than reusing its scope/hash. Staged semantic variants use the same proposal shape after canonical acceptance.

Under S05 gate and canonical lock order, reauthorize this predicate, check If-Match/expected semantic epoch/prior decisions and exact releases, then use C14 for semantic branches. Increment document revision, append audit/review decision + operation result, commit and fsync C16 authority checkpoint before201. Classification uses the same authority/checkpoint path; any semantic consequences also append C14 invalidations in that transaction. Authorized stale subject/revision gives409; inaccessible/nonexistent subject gives indistinguishable404. Unknown commit/checkpoint outcome gives503 and sealed recovery, never an optimistic success. Replays return the same decision refs only after current authorization; no duplicate event or capability widening. SQL review-decision subject references use the strict staged/published union with composite ownership FKs/deferred integrity validation. Published inspection uses ordinary reader RLS; no staged OR exception or new privileged content-reader role is added.

T06 MUST publish R/F125 first, authorize this actual route without a package, retract/correct/undo during buffering while bytes/R/vector stay unchanged, and verify current filters plus final response rejection. Include denied peer, wrong release/tenant, forged dependency, stale epoch/prior decision, same-key replay/conflict and classification authority negatives. A direct fixture/projection update is insufficient API evidence.

Idempotent published-review ordering: validate the tagged body and current subject/source/review authorization, resolve its C16 operation/scope/digest, then return a currently authorized **committed** matching outcome before testing optimistic preconditions for a new mutation. A successful retry therefore does not fail merely because its own first commit advanced document/semantic revisions. A changed digest conflicts; an inaccessible source/result denies; an unresolved outcome seals/reconciles. Only a genuinely new operation evaluates If-Match/expected epoch/prior decisions and appends events.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: A `ContractFamily` is tenant-scoped `family_id, custodian_id, revision, membership_revision, membership_hash, current_applicability_set_id|null`. `revision` is the family command CAS revision; `membership_revision` is a separate monotonic Epoch for the complete registered-instrument head. External contract numbers are accepted observations, never the primary key. A family contains separate independently published documents of kind original/amendment/appendix/replacement and may register a pending unpublished instrument. Each instrument retains its own source replacement history and read grants. Uploading payment amendment M does not retire original O. An appendix embedded in O is evidence within O; a separately uploaded appendix is a separate document. `amendment_of`, `appendix_of` and `replaces` are reviewed relations with evidence, not automatic effects of filenames or ordinal.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: `ApplicabilitySet` is an immutable reviewer-approved manifest: `set_id, family_id, revision, membership_revision, membership_hash, semantic_epoch, recorded_at, prior_set_id|null, reviewer_decision_ids[], status=accepted|unknown|conflicting, members[], scopes[], decision_evidence_ids[]`. Manifest status is its immutable approval judgment; current trust is a separate C14 acceptance projection with state `accepted|unknown|conflicting|invalidated`, so invalidation never edits a historical manifest. Member: `document_id, consideration=pending|applicable|supplemental|excluded|conflicting, version_id|null, extraction_id|null, release_id|null, role, asserted_valid_from/to, reviewed_valid_from/to, date_basis, relation_decision_id|null, review_decision_id|null, reason_code|null, evidence_ids[]`. Only pending may lack a published release/decision; applicable/supplemental/excluded/conflicting bind exact published source identities and reviewed evidence. Exclusion needs a reason and evidence, not omission. Scope: `scope_key, interval:[from,to), state=accepted|unknown|conflicting, base_evidence_ids[], effects[]`. Effect: `kind=preserve|supersede|supplement|exclude, target_scope_key, source_evidence_ids[], supersedes_effect_ids[], effective_from/to, reviewer_decision_id`. Unknown bounds mean unknown unless a reviewer explicitly marks them unbounded. Interval end is exclusive; LocalDate uses approved family jurisdiction timezone (proposed Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh), recorded time stays UTC. No implicit legal interpretation is delegated to the clock.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: `FamilyMembershipRevision={family_id,membership_revision,membership_hash,prior_membership_revision|null,entries[],registration_decision_ids[]}` is an immutable full manifest. Each entry is exactly one `document_id,instrument_kind,relation_state=pending|reviewed,relation_decision_id|null,current_release_id|null`. Hash is SHA-256 of the RFC8785 manifest body excluding its own hash, with entries sorted by document UUID. Membership history is append-only: withdrawal records an explicit authorized decision and removes the entry only from the **next** current manifest; no earlier registry/set is edited. Known means registered with this family, including pending sources/relations; this contract cannot discover never-supplied documents. The server compares applicability member IDs against all current membership entries in **both set directions**, disallowing omitted, duplicate and foreign members. Future-effective amendments are included now, with reviewed intervals; they do not disappear from the inventory before their date. Any pending member or unknown effect prevents accepted global current applicability; conflicting members make the set conflicting. Source quotations remain usable independently without a completeness claim.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: Review must cover the base scope inventory (original clause/obligation keys), including explicit `preserve` for unchanged scopes. A partial amendment supersedes **only named scopes**, not the entire original. Supplement adds conjunction evidence, never silently overwrites. Full replacement must explicitly exclude/supersede all prior applicable scopes for the stated interval. Overlapping competing supersessions require an explicit reviewed precedence decision with evidence; lacking it the scope is conflicting. Future effects are present but not yet effective. Unknown date/target/precedence yields unknown/conflicting, not upload-order wins. Scope keys are SHA-256 of a versioned RFC8785 tuple `(family_id,clause_identity,party_role,obligation_kind,currency,tax_basis,installment_id,due_condition_identity)`; unknown components remain tagged unknown and cannot imply equality with a known scope. Clause identity alignment between extractions requires a reviewed mapping.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: Current-obligation query pins set ID, membership revision/hash, semantic epoch and evaluation date, selects accepted effects whose half-open intervals contain that date, applies only reviewed scoped supersession and assembles AND evidence for original clause, amendment and its condition/qualifiers. For example O has warranty W and payment P; M supersedes P with P2 from date D; A supplements P2 with condition C. At D the sufficient bundles are `{O.W}` for warranty and `{O.P,M.P2,A.C,precedence decision evidence}` for payment. Before D the payment bundle remains `{O.P}`. A second unresolved M2 does not win because it uploaded last. No new consolidated source text is manufactured.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: Reviewer/publisher needs family-management authority **and inspection/read authority for every supporting instrument**. Current legal composition requires the caller to read all members/decision-evidence dependencies of the selected set, including sources used to resolve conflicts/exclusions. This conservative conjunction prevents claiming a globally complete obligation using a hidden amendment. If unavailable, return generic insufficient current-obligation outcome, without hidden names/counts/reasons. Independent authorized source excerpts can still be searched as references with applicability unknown. Do not call them a complete legal answer. History capability is not required for unchanged clauses of still-active original O; retired source releases still need history and cannot be made current solely by a family edge.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: APIs: POST `/contract-families` creates an empty family under management capability; GET `/contract-families/{id}` returns only a fully permitted manifest (no partial member counts); POST `/contract-families/{id}/applicability-sets` accepts expected family/semantic revision, exact published members, scope effects and reviewed decision refs. Under S05 gate, lock family/documents, validate same-tenant ownership/current releases/permissions/intervals/coverage, append set+dependencies, CAS family pointer, advance semantic/corpus epochs and root revision; commit or409. Unknown/conflicting sets may be recorded but cannot produce supported current-obligation claims. A source replacement invalidates/rebinds dependent sets in its publication transaction; retraction/deletion invalidates them immediately. Citation reconstruction records family/set/effect/decision IDs **and every exact physical source release/evidence ID**; evidence endpoint never retargets O to M. A stale set citation may show exact source as a labeled reference if independently permitted, but cannot assert the old applicability decision is still current.

requirements.section: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: SQL additions: `contract_families`, `family_membership_revisions` and `family_memberships` (immutable complete head manifests and their entries), `applicability_sets`, `applicability_members` and `applicability_effects` with T-composite FKs, unique family revision, validated typed scope/interval payload and reverse evidence dependencies. Current set FK is deferrable; membership registration/change/withdrawal and source-head change invalidate or completely replace the active set transactionally under the RR02 rule below. These are not a second contract-content store. Historical versions using amendment/appendix relation must be split into independent instruments with reviewed mappings; old URLs stay old references, not silently reassigned. No actual enterprise corpus exists to migrate in this task.

requirements.section: Membership mutation and stale-set fencing — RR02 / T02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: POST `/contract-families/{id}/memberships` accepts the strict command `{action:register|update_relation|withdraw,document_id,expected_membership_revision,expected_membership_hash,registration_decision_id,relation_decision_id|null,reason_code,replacement_set|null}` plus If-Match family `revision` and Idempotency-Key. Family management and current inspection authority over every registered instrument are required: published sources use read/history policy, pending sources require a current safe C11 package. A register may remain pending; it never asserts legal precedence. The response returns only a fully permitted manifest or opaque operation refs, never partial counts or hidden names.

requirements.section: Membership mutation and stale-set fencing — RR02 / T02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: Under S05 gate → tenant heads → affected families → documents, validate current identity/all-source authority, CAS both family/membership heads and append the complete next membership manifest. Register, withdrawal, accepted relation change, or member source publication/replacement/tombstone **always** advances membership revision/hash, family revision, semantic epoch and retention-root revision. In the same transaction close the current applicability acceptance interval/append `applicability_invalidate`, and clear its current pointer, unless `replacement_set` is a completely validated set bound to the new head. It may be unknown/conflicting but cannot support a current legal claim. C14 relation decisions and C02 publication MUST invoke this rule, even when the old set has no dependency edge to the new member. No independent membership-row edits are permitted. The transaction adopts the new membership-head retention root/dependency manifest before removing the prior current-head root; citation/history/records roots remain independent. Journal/checkpoint before Ack follows C16. Family registration before first publication therefore makes incompleteness explicit instead of preserving an old accepted answer.

requirements.section: Membership mutation and stale-set fencing — RR02 / T02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: POST `/contract-families/{id}/applicability-sets` additionally requires expected membership revision/hash and complete `members[]`; it checks exact server-known membership equality, current source-head equality, reviewed disposition/effects/intervals, all-source rights and expected semantic/family revisions before pointer CAS. Accepted sets require no pending/conflicting member, every membership entry relation_state=reviewed with a current published release, fully reviewed exclusions, covered base scopes and no unknown/conflicting applicable scope. Applicability submission cannot silently approve a still-pending registry relation; that change uses the atomic membership transition. Future applicable/supplemental members can be accepted with reviewed effective intervals. Final legal claim/citation validation checks `(family_id,set_id,membership_revision,membership_hash)` against **both** current family membership and current accepted-set pointer, plus current semantic acceptance and every member/decision dependency. A fresh tenant epoch cannot make S1 current after M2 joins. If the full set is not permitted, return the same generic insufficient outcome; no partial manifest or hidden-member explanation. Ordinary authorized excerpts keep applicability unknown.

requirements.section: Membership mutation and stale-set fencing — RR02 / T02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: Relational additions: `family_management_assignments(T,id,family_id,principal_id?|group_id?,purpose_id,valid_from,valid_to?,revision)` with XOR subject and tenant/family/principal/group FKs; only trusted provisioner commands through S05 change these assignments and advance auth epoch. `family_membership_revisions(T,id,family_id,membership_revision,membership_hash,prior_revision?,registration_decision_ids[],cause_operation_id)` has PK(T,id), UNIQUE(T,family_id,membership_revision) and deferred same-tenant FK to authority_operations for its committing cause. `family_memberships` has PK(T,family_id,membership_revision,document_id) with role/relation state/current release and ownership FKs. The full immutable membership manifest is reconstructed from these SQL rows; **no document-owned artifact FK is required for a family or empty family head**. Its SQL surrogate id/cause are provenance outside the logical C12 manifest hash. A family_membership retention root targets this head's UUID and traverses its registered source/decision dependencies. Applicability sets FK to `(T,family_id,membership_revision)` and carry the same hash; deferred integrity validation enforces hash/complete-manifest/member equality and exact source ancestry. Pending members have null release identity; nonpending identity fields are all present, with ownership FKs. The family current-set FK validates same family and membership head, not merely same tenant. Historical membership revisions and invalidated sets remain immutable audit/retention objects, not authority. Migration0004 creates these declarations; release FKs attach in0006 before any family traffic.

requirements.section: Membership mutation and stale-set fencing — RR02 / T02
requirements.parent: C12 Contract families and applicability sets — HR02
requirements.text: T02 includes O/M1/S1 accepted, then register pending M2: the same transaction invalidates S1. A new request at the new semantic epoch is still insufficient. Test M2 conflict, future effect, reviewed exclusion, stale/omitted/duplicate membership, withdrawal, concurrent source replacement and a reader denied M2. Only a complete newly accepted permitted set may restore legal completeness.

`ServingProfile` is immutable `profile_id, retrieval_profile_hash, mode=lexical|hybrid, embedding_space_id|null, query_encoder_manifest_id|null, chunker_profile_hash, lexical_compiler_hash, fusion_hash, packing_tokenizer="unicode-scalar-v1", state=shadow|validated|retired`. Embedding space includes exact weights/model **revision**, tokenizer, runtime, dtype, pooling, normalization, query/passage prefixes, dimension and config digests (C06). Equal dimension does not establish compatibility. Mode lexical has no encoder; mode hybrid requires exactly one compatible space for **all** served members. No per-document choice of query encoder and no cross-space cosine comparisons.

`CorpusRevision` is an immutable complete membership manifest `revision, profile_id, prior_revision|null, member_manifest_hash, source_head_hash, semantic_epoch_at_validation, created_at`, with rows `(document_id,release_id,rendition_id,generation_id,space_id|null)` for **every eligible active published rendition**. Serving-profile state remains validated while selected by the head; there is no undeclared active enum. A chosen complete generation becomes published when its corpus revision activates; unused old representations retire only when no active/in-flight/rollback root needs them. Authorization joins the **C13 selected generation**, not the initial release_members provenance generation, whose retirement cannot hide an otherwise active source. Same-source generations may coexist; `(release_id,rendition_id,generation_id)` validation proves extraction/source maps match. `tenants.active_serving_profile_id + corpus_revision` is one atomic head; source publication/deletion atomically creates the next membership revision. A generation is replaceable representation, a release is source identity; model changes no longer rewrite source releases.

`ResponseSnapshot` required fields: `auth_epoch, corpus_epoch, semantic_epoch, corpus_revision` (Epoch strings), `policy_revision, serving_profile_id, deployment_incarnation` (UUIDs), `journal_sequence` (Epoch), `evaluated_at, valid_until` (UTC Instant; valid_until is the conservative earliest permission/source/set boundary or request deadline), `releases[]` exact `{document_id,version_id,extraction_id,rendition_id,release_id,generation_id}`, `applicability_sets[]` exact `{family_id,applicability_set_id,membership_revision,membership_hash}`. Query encoder/space is resolved from immutable serving profile, never a caller choice. C14 resolves the semantic event head for this epoch. All returned payload objects include only permitted refs; snapshot does not expose inaccessible family IDs/members. A legal-template claim additionally requires `applicability_set_id, effect_ids[], decision_ids[]`; excerpts may omit those fields but must not assert legal completeness. Published citation resolution rechecks the set/current trust if rendering a legal claim.

SQL additions: `serving_profiles`, `corpus_revisions`, `corpus_members`, `migration_runs` (target profile/base revision/watermark/state/counts/reservation), with T-composite keys/FKs and indexes by revision/release and generation. Corpus-member unique key `(T,corpus_revision,release_id,rendition_id)` enforces one selected generation. Validator compares the exact eligible-source set to members (anti-join in both directions), ownership, artifact hashes, count per source, vector completeness, space identity and current deny/tombstone state. A profile cannot filter out incomplete docs to pass completeness. A not-yet-published upload is not an eligible source; an already published source must remain covered.
Migration A→B:

1. Keep A+query encoder A serving. Reserve measured model/RAM/DB/WAL/disk/backup overlap, minimum free headroom and operator cancel plan before shadow work. Build B from exact immutable source revisions under job fences. Queries never use shadow B.

2. Publications during shadowing must complete A representations; they advance corpus head and enqueue B delta. Delete immediately denies/removes source from A and B candidate membership, even if B workers finish late. Source replacement drops old membership; shadow targets exact new release. Missing B merely delays migration, never removes A content. Semantic corrections follow C14; source-only vectors remain valid.

3. Outside the gate, reserve memory, load and prewarm the exact compatible query encoder B and validate its manifest/runtime; failure leaves A serving. Then briefly under S05 gate + tenant head lock, reconcile B against the latest source head, revalidate exact completeness and policy/deny state and the already-prewarmed encoder identity/readiness, then CAS **one corpus head** to B and append roots/audit. If source head or encoder readiness changed, fail/reconcile outside the gate; no partial cutover or model load/prewarm inside the gate.

4. Requests pin `(profile_id,corpus_revision,space_id)` and may finish retrieval with encoder A. Pilot final guard rejects a retired serving profile as409 `STALE_SNAPSHOT`; unrelated membership revisions may preserve positive used-source validity per C16, but it does not dispatch old-profile results or automatically rerun under a new principal/snapshot. Old A encoder/representations remain rooted until all bounded requests finish and the approved rollback window expires.

5. Rollback constructs a **new** corpus revision using old profile A only after it covers today's eligible releases and current denies/applicability/semantics. New documents since cutover need A backfill before rollback; otherwise remain on B or fail closed. Never restore an old membership snapshot that resurrects a deletion. Deletes must purge all representations, including rollback ones.

If both encoders cannot fit even briefly, do **not** promise online migration: schedule an approved maintenance operation that publishes a complete lexical profile for the whole corpus, drains requests, unloads A, builds/prewarms B, switches to complete B. Label lexical mode and report semantic capability unavailable; full semantic SLO is suspended only under that approved window. Old-profile rollback may require maintenance too. CPU-first budget is preserved; no extra vector DB/model fleet is implied. On ordinary query-time encoder failure, keep full profile membership and return explicitly degraded lexical results across the entire eligible corpus, not dense hits from only a convenient subset.

requirements.section: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.parent: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.text: Choose a **monotonic tenant semantic epoch**, append-only events and acceptance intervals; no mutable forever-accepted row. `SemanticEvent={event_id,epoch,kind=fact_accept|fact_retract|fact_correct|link_accept|link_undo|relation_accept|relation_retract|applicability_accept|applicability_invalidate,subject_ids[],prior_event_ids[],decision_id,dependency_ids[],recorded_at}`. One transaction may append several events at one new epoch. `SemanticSnapshot={epoch,event_head_hash}` resolves the exact accepted intervals at that epoch. Current SQL projections are rebuildable from the immutable event chain; acceptance interval is `accepted_at_epoch≤e AND (retracted_at_epoch IS NULL OR e<retracted_at_epoch)` plus known/evidence/scope validation. A correction appends a new observation and retract/accept events, never edits historical literal evidence. Entity-link undo and scope/validity corrections use the same mechanism.

requirements.section: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.parent: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.text: Semantic transaction: authority gate → tenant serving/semantic/lifecycle head locks → affected families then documents in UUID order → validate reviewer/rule/policy/exact source/dependencies and expected epoch → close acceptance intervals/append replacements/events → rebuild trusted exact fact/entity projection, invalidate affected applicability/derived objects (family-membership relations also run the C12 membership-head transition) → increment semantic epoch, corpus epoch if eligibility changes and retention-root revision → audit/outbox → commit. Publication binds `semantic_epoch_at_publication` as provenance; it never freezes trust indefinitely. Rule-acceptance code uses the same path. Retracting a fact does not wait for re-embedding or a replacement source release.

requirements.section: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.parent: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.text: Baseline searchable contextual text/sketches are **literal source-derived only**. Accepted semantic values/links cannot be baked into baseline vectors or source snippets as independent truth. Exact fact/entity channels join current semantic snapshot live. Optional derived semantic sketches must declare event/epoch dependencies; a retraction immediately makes them unavailable and promotion requires an atomic replacement/profile-completeness contract. They are disabled in the pilot, avoiding loss of an otherwise eligible source while such a projection rebuilds. Literal canonical clause text remains searchable as a quote, explicitly distinct from a trusted retracted fact.

requirements.section: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.parent: C14 Semantic decisions and accepted snapshots — HR06
requirements.text: All internal cache keys include tenant/principal/purpose/auth epoch/policy/source refs/semantic epoch/profile/corpus revision/compiler/packing identity; pending denies are checked even on a cache hit. Answer caches are disabled initially; pooled authorization sets are request-transaction local. Final response validates current semantic epoch and every used fact/link/set acceptance/dependency. If 125 was accepted during retrieval and retracted while answer buffered, epoch mismatch discards the buffered answer, even though source hash/release/vector is unchanged. No asynchronous outbox delivery is required for safety. Coarse semantic invalidation is an intentional pilot simplicity; T12 measures its stale/error cost rather than claiming free concurrency.

requirements.section: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.parent: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.text: `QueryPlan={revision:"query-v1",compiler_profile:"vi-en-or-v1",packing_tokenizer:"unicode-scalar-v1",slots:[{slot_id,ordinal,kind,required,preserved_identifiers[],condition_terms[],query_variants[]}],filters,scope,evaluated_at}`. At most3 slots, original +≤2 approved deterministic alias variants per slot. Unknown decomposition/ambiguous party or more than3 required slots yields clarification/partial with no inferred missing clause. Negation and conditions are preserved slot constraints, not disposable fillers. Same principal/time/filters/profile across every channel. Generated rewrite/HyDE remain optional disabled arms.

requirements.section: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.parent: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.text: Lexical compiler `vi-en-or-v1` is deterministic and frozen with its glossary/stop-list hashes. Extract protected ID literals (leading zeros/slash/hyphen/issuer retained); accepted exact-ID resolution is separate from FTS and ambiguous IDs never become a hard filter. Tokenize remaining NFC text using PostgreSQL `simple` lexemes, max32 unique terms in source order. Remove only versioned **whole phrase** fillers `xin cho biết`, `cho biết`, `vui lòng`, `please tell me`, `please`, `what is`; never globally drop `không`, `chưa`, `trừ`, `nếu`, `unless`, `not`, `except`, `if` or numeric/date/unit terms. Keep original and separately folded lowercase/diacritic/đ→d forms. Longer meaningful questions beyond32 terms request clarification rather than silent semantic truncation. Empty content with an exact accepted identifier uses exact-only; otherwise asks clarification.

requirements.section: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.parent: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.text: Candidate query is OR of safely constructed single-term `plainto_tsquery('simple', parameter)` nodes combined by typed SQL tsquery OR, **never** an all-question AND and never interpolated user tsquery operators. Original/folded/aliases merge by maximum within-channel ranking tuple `(distinct content lexemes matched, explicit quoted-phrase/proximity match, ts_rank_cd(normalization32), stable source tie)` with token-position phrase checks. Quoted phrases boost, not an obligatory exact match unless an explicit exact filter was requested. English morphology uses only reviewed deterministic glossary aliases in this baseline, with no undocumented stemming; separate English/VI-segmented/BM25 compilers are measured E02 arms. Negation may broaden candidate retrieval but EvidenceGate must verify the full literal condition; it cannot strip an exception to declare support. This OR compiler intentionally trades precision for candidate recall, to be measured T09/E02. Parameters, length/deadline and authorized source relation constrain cost.

requirements.section: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.parent: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.text: Per slot retrieve exact20 / lexical40 / dense40. Original/folded/alias lists merge **within** the lexical40 budget; document-sketch expansion also consumes lexical40 (at most10 child candidates), adding no votes/channel. Fuse per slot RRF60, one vote/chunk/channel after variant merge, deterministic ties C07/algorithm defaults. Cap each slot union at100, including sketches; no unbounded fanout. Exact tier applies only to unambiguous accepted authorized identifier resolution. Allocate global120 **by round-robin over slot ordinals**, one next unique chunk from each slot per pass; skip duplicate IDs without consuming capacity, record their membership for every matched slot; refill until120 or exhaustion. With 3 disjoint 100 lists each slot gets 40; with 1 gets at most100; a short slot's unused allocation is automatically available to others. Preserve slot membership through rerank/dedup. Within-slot duplicates do not gain votes; shared candidates can cover several slots. Rerank optional top20 from the admitted pool, never recover a dropped candidate by implication. Track raw/admitted/final recall per slot.

requirements.section: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.parent: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.text: `/search.top_k=1..20` counts unique search hits after fair admission/dedup; final hit selection cycles slot lists in the same stable order. `/answers.top_k` bounds the displayed supporting hit list only, **not** the independent evidence resolver; it may include additional cited qualifiers. Answer packing allows≤10 seed children (two/parent, third only to complete a required slot), plus dependency expansion. Pack complete source-supported bundles, not arbitrary top-k passages. Deterministic packing tokenizer `unicode-scalar-v1` counts each Unicode scalar as one packing token, including titles, citation labels, separators and qualifiers; parent≤900, total≤2400. This deliberately conservative, model-independent unit is **not an E5 token count**. A future generator must add its own measured tokenizer limit, never reinterpret2400 silently. Prefer bundles covering more required slots, then fewer packing tokens, then fused order; include all AND qualifiers or omit that bundle. Required bundle too large→partial/insufficient `EVIDENCE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, never cut exception/units to fit. Metadata/source snippets are within256KiB final payload.

requirements.section: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.parent: C15 Query plans, lexical compilation and budgets — HR08/HR09
requirements.text: Lexical-only chunker `lexical-cp-v1` needs no model: body target1280 code points, total≤1920 including context≤384, overlap≤160 within same section/scope; split on sentence/row boundary, then safe scalar boundaries with explicit source maps. E5 chunker remains actual-token320/480/40. They have different chunker/generation identities; lexical success never supplies fake E5 counts. Compare both with common evidence gold and packing budget. Profiles carry exact compiler/allocator/chunker/packing hashes; changes invalidate cached plans and benchmark comparability.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Authoritative live journal is an encrypted append-only local filesystem ledger on approved durable storage **outside SQL backup rollback**, owned only by the S05 singleton process. No sidecar appenders, independent writer tool or multiple hosts. `operation_id` is a server-issued UUID for one logical command; `record_id` is a different UUID for one immutable ledger record. Common record fields: `record_id,entry_kind,operation_id,tenant_id,sequence,command_digest,idempotency_scope_digest,digest_key_revision,previous_entry_hash,entry_hash,created_at`. Sequence is the globally contiguous ledger Epoch; **record idempotency is UNIQUE(tenant_id,entry_kind,operation_id)**, not global operation-ID record uniqueness. A delete normally owns one deny_intent and one authority_commit with different record IDs/sequences. Records contain no content/filenames. Command/scope digests are versioned keyed private digests of normalized typed command and `(tenant,principal,route,Idempotency-Key)`; raw keys or corrected semantic values are not journal payload. Create/rotate segments with file+directory fsync; append complete length/checksummed record then fsync before durable acknowledgement/deny installation. The singleton owns the exclusive OS lock for its whole lifetime and reads through a validated contiguous head, not a lagging subscription. Access is authenticated through the normal mutation route; local file ACL/encryption protects privileged operator access.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: During the append/install/SQL path the S05 gate blocks all affected egress. Every final read/preview/download dispatch checks the current in-memory deny set plus validated journal head; there is no stale TTL authorization or deny cache. Journal read health/fsync failure/unknown append outcome poisons **all content-serving readiness**, not just one document. SQL tombstone is a query prefilter/projection; durable journal deny overrides SQL rollback. Candidate/exact/entity SQL joins a trusted request-local eligible-source relation minus the current journal deny set **before text/value selection**; a new head during work triggers fresh dependency denies at expansion/model-input and final dispatch. Raw journal state never comes from client parameters. This service overlay is required in addition to SQL RLS, which cannot observe a failed SQL journal projection. A second API process cannot obtain the OS lock and MUST fail startup before serving (T05 tests this as the second-reader outcome). Multiple reader replicas, NFS lock assumptions and automatic cross-host takeover are unsupported; expanding this envelope requires a new live-consistency protocol.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Restart/reconciliation: exclusive lock plus confirmed predecessor death/closed listener; verify authenticated saved journal head/anchor, contiguous hash chain and final segment; then replay all intents into SQL before readiness, compare SQL heads against latest authority_commit checkpoints, obtain current identity/key watermarks and reconstruct denies/roots. A normal process restart with current SQL reconciles committed-but-unacknowledged operations from immutable events/idempotency/outbox and creates a verified checkpoint; it does not assume a restored snapshot is current. Hash chain alone does not detect complete-file rollback: operator-maintained independent head/backup inventory must agree; missing anchor/segment/tail corruption or ambiguous fsync tail requires sealed recovery from verified backup, never truncate-and-serve. Entries are not dropped merely because tombstone committed. Every acknowledged visible mutation also fsyncs a content-free `authority_commit` checkpoint in this **same ledger** after SQL commit, containing operation/tenant IDs, authority_revision, auth/semantic/corpus revisions and their head hashes, policy/key revision and deployment incarnation. Failure/unknown checkpoint durability seals serving and withholds Ack. The append format is a strict tagged union: deny_intent uses the document/reason fields above; authority_commit uses these head fields; both share sequence/previous hash/timestamp. This detects local-grant/semantic rollback that a delete-only replay cannot detect. Compaction requires verified archive/head plus proof no restorable snapshot can predate the retained floor; default pilot has **no journal compaction**. Host/storage loss invokes sealed manual disaster recovery with approved RPO/RTO; no unsupported multi-host availability claim.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: If SQL is **behind an acknowledged authority checkpoint** after backup restore/failover, there is no trusted log of every grant/fact value to replay from metadata alone. Pilot recovery therefore stays sealed and uses a conservative **fresh approval** path: retain originals/history privately; append invalidations for every restored local grant/session/reviewer assignment, accepted semantic/applicability decision and serving source/profile head. Rebuild indexes/coverage from surviving verified sources and reapprove fresh reviewers/readers/facts/family sets/publications using current accountable authorities, with durable denies always overriding. No restored grant or fact is accepted merely because it was accepted in the backup. An approved complete current policy/semantic operation backup could support a later replay design, but it is not assumed available. A09/A05 must explicitly accept this slower manual recovery before dependent acceptance; that approval is pending. If they reject it, the production recovery design must be revisited. This avoids silent resurrection of post-snapshot grant revocations or fact retractions without adding another database.

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: The strict record union has exactly two branches. `deny_intent` adds `document_id,requested_by_id,reason_code,expected_document_revision`; it durably authorizes only irreversible deny/tombstone reconciliation for that target, not unrelated writes. `authority_commit` adds `authority_revision,auth_epoch,semantic_epoch,corpus_epoch,corpus_revision,auth_head_hash,semantic_head_hash,corpus_head_hash,policy_revision,key_revision,deployment_incarnation,result_ref,intent_record_id|null`. Delete commits MUST link their same-operation intent; other commands use null. Same-kind/same-operation/same immutable payload replay returns the **same** record ID/sequence/hash without appending; a changed payload/scope returns409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` and never changes the deny. Retrying a durable record cannot synthesize a new timestamp/record ID. The second kind is a new record, not a duplicate of the first. Hashing/checksums cover tag and all immutable fields.

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: `entry_hash = SHA256(RFC8785(record without entry_hash))`; the previous hash and record tag/identity are included. Command/scope digest canonicalization and key revision are pinned independently of record hashing. A matching committed SQL operation is an idempotent result path, not a new CAS attempt against the already-advanced epoch. Missing/unknown checkpoint still seals before returning a successful mutation result.

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: The authority reconstructs its scope→operation and typed-record indexes from the contiguous journal at startup. A delete resolves or allocates its operation ID before appending its first intent; the durable scope/digest in that intent makes intent-only retry stable even if the SQL registration failed. SQL `authority_operations(T,operation_id,command_digest,idempotency_scope_digest,digest_key_revision,kind,result_ref,committed_authority_revision,head_manifest)` is UNIQUE(T,operation_id) and UNIQUE(T,idempotency_scope_digest), inserted **in the mutation transaction**. It stores immutable committed outcome refs/heads, not an independent mutable acceptance flag. These operation rows and ledger idempotency indexes are retained for the ledger/recovery lifetime; the ordinary seven-day HTTP replay window does not permit their reuse or duplicate mutation. Scope lookup checks **all retained digest-key revisions before allocating** an operation, and recomputes a matched command digest under its original key revision. Rotation retains protected old lookup keys or a verified equivalent rotation index for that lifetime; missing lookup capability seals affected mutation readiness rather than treating an old key as a new command. Authenticated result replay reauthorizes; an actor who lost rights cannot read results. Recovery still completes an already-authorized irreversible deny as the trusted reconciler, with audit, even if its original requester is now revoked.

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: | No durable intent and no committed SQL operation | No accepted delete. A current authorized retry may create the operation/intent. Unknown/torn append is not this state: seal until verified ledger recovery. |

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: | Intent durable, SQL definitely rolled back | Deny stays installed; 503+operation ref/deny_durable. Against verified-current SQL, reconcile tombstone under the same operation and insert its SQL outcome once. No physical purge yet. |

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: | SQL outcome committed, authority_commit missing/uncertain | No Ack; seal. Verify ledger tail/anchor and SQL operation/head against independent acknowledged checkpoints. A verified missing commit record is appended/fsynced once from the committed outcome; never reapply fact/grant/delete mutations. An uncertain tail stays sealed until verified recovery. |

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: | Authority_commit durable, Ack lost | The typed-record and SQL operation keys return the existing outcome after current authorization. No second epoch increment, event, tombstone or checkpoint record. |

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: | SQL snapshot behind any acknowledged checkpoint | Use the C16 sealed fresh-approval recovery path; absence of an operation in stale SQL is **not** proof it never committed. Replay durable denies, invalidate restored authority/trust/heads, rebuild/reapprove with new operations/incarnation; do not replay old semantic/grant commands as new. |

requirements.section: Journal record union and operation recovery — RR03 / T05
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: During sealed fresh-approval recovery, retain the verified ledger/head and operation identities, set new SQL authority/auth/semantic/corpus counters above their recorded high-water values and issue a new deployment incarnation. Record the recovery's invalidations/new heads as a new authority operation/checkpoint before readiness; an old operation's retry cannot adopt a changed payload/head. Missing journal/anchor or uncertain predecessor death still forbids readiness. T05 must exercise both records for one delete, same-kind stable replay, digest conflict, intent-only retry, committed-outcome recovery, lost Ack and behind-checkpoint restore. Finite models do not establish actual fsync/SQL/transport durability.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Roots: all active source releases, current accepted semantic facts/links/relations, **current family membership-head manifests and every registered entry/registration/relation decision dependency, including pending instruments even without a current applicability set**, accepted/unknown/conflicting current applicability manifests and every member/decision evidence, active serving membership, in-flight request pins, staged review packages/jobs until expiry/completion, retained citations, approved rollback profiles/releases within window, accepted-original records schedule and legal holds. Traverse **both** evidence dependency edges to exact source/element/extraction and artifact dependency edges to original/raw/maps/previews/representations. Enrichment/source diagrams alone are not a retention inventory. Root kind is the closed enum `source|semantic|family_membership|applicability|serving|request|review_job|citation|rollback|records|hold`. Store `retention_roots(T,root_kind,root_id,target_kind,target_id,expires_at?,revision)` and an indexed typed `dependency_edges` view over evidence/artifact graphs; validate all endpoints and cycles. Roots preserve bytes, never confer ordinary read authority. Persisted/published citations are active roots until explicit expiry/withdrawal; root removal transaction marks the citation expired/unavailable before GC may claim its evidence. Transient response references are valid only under their snapshot/source validity and reauthorize on resolution, not perpetual published citation objects. No still-active published citation/fact may survive as resolvable after evidence purge.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Artifact processing state remains exactly C06 `staged|verified|adopted|purged`. Separate `artifact_gc(T,artifact_id,state=live|gc_pending|purging|purged,revision,marked_root_revision?,claim_id?)` has PK/FK(T,artifact_id), one row per artifact from registration and index(T,state,revision). `live` means no GC exclusion, not read authorization. `gc_claims(T,id,artifact_id,document_id,kind=tombstone|retention,target_manifest_hash,root_revision,gc_revision,hold_revision,tombstone_revision?,operation_id,state=issued|completed)` binds a validated immutable list of exact storage keys/**versions** and private manifests, with composite ownership and one active claim per artifact. Manifest targets are server-generated, never caller paths. Completion mirrors artifact processing state to purged and GC state to purged in one authority transaction. These are explicit migration0002/0007 declarations, not new extraction quality states.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: GC two stages: under S05 gate/tenant lifecycle lock, mark only expired unreachable unheld retention targets `live→gc_pending`, recording root revision and removing availability for new publication/review. A tombstone target additionally needs confirmed SQL tombstone; explicit access deletion may override ordinary serving roots but never a physical records/hold prohibition. New roots cannot reference pending/purging/purged artifacts. A pending mark may be cancelled `gc_pending→live` only under that lock, before any claim, after revalidating surviving bytes and eligibility; otherwise publication fails409 or rebuilds a new identity. The singleton rechecks roots/retention/hold/current tombstone and target ownership, then CASes `gc_pending→purging` and issues the exact claim. Physical version deletion runs **outside** the gate; purging cannot return to live or accept a new root. Failure stays purging with same-claim idempotent retry. Verified physical absence permits `purging→purged`; no file-delete success is inferred from a storage delete marker alone. TTL alone never authorizes GC.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: `rag_purger` has no general content SELECT, SQL DELETE/UPDATE, arbitrary object listing/key deletion, claim issuance or publication privileges. It may fetch only an assigned issued claim's bounded target manifest and submit absence/failure receipts through fixed constrained functions. The trusted storage broker deletes only those exact versions under a currently issued purging claim; API singleton alone adopts claims/completion. `kind=tombstone` requires confirmed tombstone plus allowed physical destruction. `kind=retention` permits expired unrooted/unheld superseded **or orphan** artifacts of a live document; it does not require tombstoning that live document. Both kinds enforce the same holds/records/ownership/fence checks, and give no permission to read held originals. Dedicated nonlogin helper ownership, locked search_path and no PUBLIC execution follow C06; no caller-chosen SQL/path is accepted.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Publication/root or hold first→GC skips/cancels pending before claim. GC claim first→publication/new root fails409; a new hold cannot promise retention of an already-purging/purged target and fails atomically with409 `HOLD_TARGET_UNAVAILABLE` plus protected operator incident/audit, rather than acknowledging a false hold. Existing holds always prevent claim; no physical deletion may start while a preexisting hold applies. Receipts/retries cannot widen target versions or change claim kind. Byte loss discovered unexpectedly invalidates dependent facts/sets/releases/profile membership under gate before any response can release, and poisons readiness until all surviving eligible sources have a complete serving profile. Requests encountering missing evidence fail closed even before repair. T10 includes actual-role forbidden mutations/paths, rooted R1 past TTL, unrooted superseded R1 of live R2, both race orders, hold-before/after-claim and physical retry/version absence.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Completed-claim identical receipt replay returns the recorded completion without another physical delete; changed targets/receipt identity conflicts. Retention orphan here means a registered attempt artifact. C09 unregistered private staging is cleaned only by its trusted intake broker against an exact owned upload/attempt manifest, serialized with registration/adoption: cleanup claimed first prevents later adoption of that key; registration first creates the artifact/root and excludes staging cleanup. This separate staging cleanup grants no arbitrary-path or published-artifact capability to rag_purger.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Explicit delete overrides serving/semantic roots for **access**, immediately invalidates dependents and removes serving pins; it may purge after SQL tombstone unless hold/records policy forbids physical destruction. Held bytes move to restricted custody and ordinary projections purge. Retention-root traversal cannot silently keep deleted facts trusted or expose held originals. If destroying cross-source evidence, invalidate accepted relationships/applicability transactionally and preserve only independent evidence of other sources. T10 tests both publication/GC orders, retained cross-source references and explicit delete+hold.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: C09 jobs add `completed_unit_keys, charged_work_seconds, charged_raster_bytes, cumulative_failures, last_quantum_at`. Persist charged budget **before** each sandbox quantum; reserve worst-case120 seconds per page/region and refund only measured unused time after successful checkpoint. Crash may overcharge, never reset. Extraction cap2700 seconds charged active work across all attempts/alternate passes (not45 min per retry); max4 execution failures, normal scheduling yields do not increment attempt. Budget exhaustion→waiting_review `EXTRACTION_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, no false ready. Operator fresh reprocess is an audited new budget allocation under tenant daily quota, not a hidden retry.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Render/process one page/region at a time, at most one current + one bounded transform scratch raster. Upload/verify/checkpoint raw/preview output before releasing page scratch. Cumulative durable bytes count against admission/storage quota; 2GiB temp is a simultaneous working-set cap, not allowance to keep all300 page rasters. Assemble canonical JSON/maps streaming with 100MiB/20M-character/cell limits, not an in-RAM full-raster list. Adapters requiring full-document resident output must prove the bound or be unsupported for long scans. After each page or120-second quantum, release parser resources/lease to a checkpoint and requeue; round-robin tenants then documents, one quantum per ready job before priority tie. Single page timeout kills group; alternate pass consumes the same cumulative budget. One long doc cannot hold the parser for45 min uninterrupted. With ≤20 runnable admitted jobs, a healthy bounded quantum gives a next-cycle scheduling bound≤40 min plus measured startup overhead; the30-min p95 queue target remains a measured workload target, not this worst-case bound. Daily1,000-page quota/global100 jobs unchanged; tests include tenant fairness and short-job progress.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Long200/300-page scans are accepted **only for bounded processing/review**, not promised automatic completion within2700 seconds. A pattern becomes supported automatic intake only after T11 establishes its budget/coverage/ready latency. Review-only/unsupported states stay in end-to-end denominators. Prototype timings cannot be inferred from mean five-page corpus.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: T12 SQL optimization resolves an authorized source/release set once per query transaction from indexed grants/membership/current semantics and joins all channels to it under RLS; it is request-local, never an authorization cache across requests. Indexed dependency closure is validated on writes, while fresh final checks retain authority. Ordinary unrelated source publications need not invalidate a positive buffered answer if its exact source releases/profile/semantic decisions remain current: validate used dependency tuples, active profile ID, auth/semantic epochs and date bounds, rather than equating any corpus-epoch increment to a rights change. Search response explicitly identifies its pinned membership revision/evaluated_at; negative/global-completeness claims require unchanged relevant corpus revision or409. Model cutover, used source changes, semantic change, deny or permission change still discard. Measure both stale rates and mutation latency under actual roles; no recursive helper performance is presumed.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: Review circuit proposed default: named primary+backup reviewer; unfinished required-review pages≤200/tenant and oldest≤1 business day during staffed hours. Breach stops **new uploads** with429 `REVIEW_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`, while existing work/reads/deletion continue. Resume only when pages<100 and age<1 day with operator acknowledgement. Forecast arrival reviewer-minutes≤80% of measured staffed service capacity over trailing5 staffed days; otherwise reduce intake. Pilot ready-to-search p95≤2 business days including review is a proposed product target, distinct from compute/queue time. T14 blind critical-value/header/party/qualifier recheck requires zero missed planted critical errors and≥99% adjudicated decision correctness on established slices; report family-clustered intervals. Sparse evidence→mandatory double review/no automation, not a spurious99% claim. Every critical disagreement blocks acceptance until independent adjudication; discovered accepted error triggers C14 retraction. The80–120-hour annotation estimate is not a capacity guarantee. Thresholds/owners require A11 ratification before operational promises.

requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: C11–C16 inherit C01 IDs/Epoch/UTC/Hash/unknown-field rejection, C06 tenant-composite FKs/FORCE RLS and C08 body/pagination limits. Package/corpus/applicability/event manifests are private server-built artifacts, never unbounded client JSON. Client applicability commands accept≤20 member IDs/≤100 effect refs per32KiB page; larger reviewed sets use staged paginated manifests and final expected-hash CAS under the same transaction, not partial publication. Review-package candidate/coverage pages≤100 items/256KiB; full protected manifest≤100MiB. Applicability and semantic typed JSON shapes list all required nullable fields above; effects and decisions require nonempty evidence on accepted state. Source/profile/semantic/GC states use closed enums; unknown values reject, not fallback. New tables have indexed referencing FKs and reverse dependency paths. P00 must materialize strict Draft2020/OpenAPI/SQL enum/ownership validators and executable round-trip cases; these prose specs and narrow SQL probes are not a complete generated service schema.

requirements.section: Consolidated contract supplements and P00 obligations
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: These clarify compatible carry-forwards and final-review integration without changing the selected architecture.

requirements.section: Consolidated contract supplements and P00 obligations
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: **Classification vocabulary and confidence.** Retain `public|internal|confidential|restricted|unknown`, with handling order public < internal < confidential < restricted and unknown handled as restricted. Type labels remain `contract|report|policy|financial_record|administrative|general|other|unknown`. Preserve separate claims/predictions/approval/effective policy; their authority rules above take precedence. The compatible shared confidence shape from revision 1 is `{raw_score:number|null, raw_scale:probability_0_1|tesseract_0_100|rule_0_1|engine_specific|not_available, grade:poor|fair|good|excellent|null, calibrated_probability:number|null, calibration_id:UUID|null}`; all keys required, unknown keys reject. All numbers are finite. Raw 0–1 scales stay within [0,1], Tesseract within [0,100], unavailable raw score is null; a nonnull calibrated probability is in [0,1] and requires matching calibration identity. This is extraction/detection confidence, distinct from the channel-score union and answer-support probability. Human approval is a decision, never a synthetic numeric confidence. Retained source: [revision-1 shared definitions](1/schemas/ragplan.schema.json); 2.2 UUID/ownership/validation rules govern their use.

requirements.section: Consolidated contract supplements and P00 obligations
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: **Deletion versus family-review authority.** A caller with current delete capability for document D can execute C10 even without family-management capability or read rights on other family instruments. The trusted authority performs mandatory membership-head advancement, current-set clearing, semantic/dependency invalidation, corpus removal, roots and checkpoint as consequences of the authorized deletion. It does not expose other members or grant the caller power to approve a replacement applicability set. The interactive `/memberships` and applicability-approval commands still require their full C12 authority. If a dependent family cannot be inspected by the caller, return only the authorized opaque deletion-operation result. T02/T05/T10 MUST cover this caller and both delete/query race orders. Trace: [final review, consumer acceptance item 4](2/review/final-review.md).

requirements.section: Consolidated contract supplements and P00 obligations
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: **Snapshot validation.** Always compare current auth and semantic epochs, policy/identity, active profile, exact used source tuples and live denies; legal claims also compare the current set pointer and membership head/hash. Broad corpus epoch changes alone need not discard a positive answer whose used dependencies remain current. Search identifies its pinned revision/time; a negative/global-completeness assertion needs unchanged relevant membership or fails stale. A new profile always discards old-profile buffers. There is no reusable authority token inferred from `valid_until`.

requirements.section: Consolidated contract supplements and P00 obligations
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: **Wire completeness before dependent acceptance.** The C contracts give exact ownership, branches, required fields, limits and behavior, but no generated 2.2 schema/OpenAPI/migration currently exists. Do not treat an old JSON example or an untyped JSONB placeholder as a completed API. P00 must enumerate every named subordinate shape (producer/normalization/coverage, locator/run range, confidence, evidence/bundle/slot, profile/config, decision subject and typed refs), all required/nullable keys, closed enums, lengths, scope-tuple unknown-component encoding, canonical-hash inputs and SQL validators; generate DTOs and round-trip them. The approved semantics and finite limits constrain that work. If an exact subordinate representation or business catalog cannot be derived without changing semantics, record the concrete unresolved interface and stop only its dependent freeze; do not invent a legal/policy default or silently accept arbitrary JSON. This is the existing RB17/CP0 schema-materialization gate, not a claim of a new Critical/High design defect.

requirements.section: Consolidated contract supplements and P00 obligations
requirements.parent: C16 Journal, retention and operational integrity — HR05/HR10/HR11/HR12/HR14
requirements.text: The journal's physical segment/anchor/encryption/key configuration, precise server transport adapter, installed dependency digests, identity mapping, records/calendar and glossary catalogs are deliberately not fabricated here.
